questions.stem: What is the equation for work done?
questions.explanation: Work done is calculated using W = Fd, where W is work done in joules, F is force in newtons, and d is distance moved in the direction of the force in metres.

questions.stem: What is the unit of work done?
questions.explanation: Work done is measured in joules (J). One joule is the work done when a force of 1 N moves an object 1 m in the direction of the force.

questions.stem: A force of 50 N pushes a box 4 m across a floor. How much work is done?
questions.explanation: W = Fd = 50 N x 4 m = 200 J.

questions.stem: A person pushes against a wall with a force of 100 N but the wall does not move. How much work is done?

options.text: It depends on the time spent pushing

questions.explanation: No work is done because the wall does not move. Work requires both a force and movement in the direction of the force (W = Fd, and d = 0).

questions.stem: When a force acts at an angle to the direction of movement, which component of force is used to calculate work?

options.text: The component in the direction of movement

questions.explanation: When force acts at an angle, only the component of force in the direction of movement does work: W = Fd cos(theta).

questions.stem: Work done against friction is transferred to which energy store?
questions.explanation: Work done against friction is transferred to the thermal energy store of the objects and surroundings, causing a temperature rise.
